## Triage: first grade · `bug` · `priority:p2` · `domain:ui` · `pm:queue` · triage seat · `session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U` · 2026-10-15T13:59Z

Read fresh. The served approval request page's highlights strip shows `submitter_id` (a `sys_user` lookup) as a bare user id. The approvals read serves `submitter_name` beside it, and the strip makes no label read. Measured on the real `RecordDetailView` under `ApprovalRecordReads`.

**Grade p2:** every approver's request page names the submitter as an id.

**Lane `domain:ui`.**

**Scope:**
- **First, the bisect the card asks for:** if the strip named the submitter before PR #12432 routed request reads through the approvals read, this is that PR's regression. Say so on the card.
- **The fix:** the lookup cell shows the served `submitter_name`, or resolves the label the way `record:highlights` resolves other lookups. One derivation, ⛔ not an approvals-only special case in the generic cell.
- **Pins:** the strip shows the name. CONTROL: a lookup with no served name still resolves through the generic path.

`finding` leaves on grading.

Claim: PM loop round 1 (`priority:p2`; triage's first grade `6193887683`)
Session: `session_01JZnppgHRp4sREcouhkQYDB`
Account: `sunhaolin`
Branch: `claude/issue-12498-submitter-name`
Worktree: `objectui-issue-12498`
Domain: `domain:ui`
Seat: `domain:ui#1`
File surface: one of the two layers the card names, chosen by the bisect and the measurement:
- (a) `apps/console/src/services/approvalRequestsDataSource.ts` and `approvalsApi.ts`, if the routed record read hands the lookup cell a shape no other record read gives it;
- (b) the `sys_user` lookup cell's resolution in `packages/fields/src/index.tsx` or `record:highlights` in `packages/plugin-detail`, only if that cell is the layer that fails for every source.

Plus the tests beside the chosen layer, and one `.changeset/12498-*.md`.

Outside the surface: objectstack's `plugin-approvals` read shape (a producer there is a cross-repo seam: stop and report), any special case keyed on `submitter_name` in a product-neutral cell (ADR-0060 rule 2), the served page's metadata, and any type, prop or export (stop on breach; explain in the report).
Container & model: `S–M`, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus` (default tier; `dispatch-gates --tier --repo objectstack-ai/objectui` names no path-derived mandate)
Clause-②: no
Responsibility:
- Whose code: this seat's PR objectui#12432 (`bedf41c1c`), if the bisect shows it is a regression of that routing. Otherwise, the lookup cell on the routed source.
- Which platform path already covers it: none for the served page. The approvals read serves `submitter_name`, and nothing reads it.
- Who reaches it: every approver who opens a served approval request page (the card's measurement on the real `RecordDetailView` under `ApprovalRecordReads`).
Thread-read: 6193887683
Serial constraints cleared: read at objectui `main` `b51242899b`.
- No `pm:dispatched` claim in objectui names `approvalRequestsDataSource.ts`, `approvalsApi.ts` or the lookup cell (scanned in this act).
- PR objectui#12541 (objectui#12523, this seat) changes `packages/fields/src/index.tsx`'s email, URL and phone cells and `HeaderHighlight.tsx`. It is in the merge queue now and lands first. If layer (b) is chosen, it is the same file in a different region, so the merge-`main` rule applies.
- The approvals face cards objectui#12489 and #12534 (queue, not dispatched) touch the same served page in other blocks.

## Closed as not planned: the premise is falsified · `domain:ui` seat 1 · `session_01JZnppgHRp4sREcouhkQYDB` · 2026-10-15T17:38Z

The dev report `6198309422` measured that the console already names the submitter. The bare id came from a test harness, not from the product. Release reason: the premise is disproved. There is no PR, and the branch `claude/issue-12498-submitter-name` was pushed empty as the claim marker.

- **Mechanism, which the seat re-read at `main`:**
  - `LookupCellRenderer` names an unexpanded id through `useLookupName` (`packages/fields/src/index.tsx:250`). That hook reads `findOne(reference, id)` from the `SchemaRendererContext` data source, not from the record's own source.
  - The console wraps every route in `SchemaRendererProvider dataSource={adapter}` (`packages/app-shell/src/console/ConsoleShell.tsx:306`).
  - So on the served `sys_approval_request_detail` page, the Submitter chip reads the `sys_user` row through the data API, which is one read per page and honours the caller's field policy, and draws the name.
- **Why the card was filed:** objectui#12482's served-page pin harness mounts `RecordDetailView` under `ApprovalRecordReads` with no root provider. There the cell has no adapter, makes 0 reads, and prints the id.
- **Bisect, same fixture:** the strip text is byte-identical on `bedf41c1c^`, on `bedf41c1c` and on `main` `165f8ff9f3`, in both trees.
  - Without the root provider, the bare id.
  - With it, as the console mounts it, the name, from 1 `sys_user` read.
  - So PR objectui#12432 caused no regression.
- **Kept behaviour:** a caller who may not read that `sys_user` row still sees today's unresolved-reference fallback (measured).
- **Not measured live:** the dev's container had no objectstack backend. So that the claim is still checked in a browser, the landing reading of the next face card on the same served page, objectui#12489, includes the Submitter chip (note on that card). If that reading shows a bare id, this card reopens.
- **Out of scope:**
  - The console's request-page pin harnesses (`apps/console/src/services/approvalRequestsDataSource.*.test.tsx`, 5 files) mount without the root provider. So a face named through the cell's own label read looks unresolved there while the console names it.
  - That is noted, not filed. It is a test-fidelity gap, not a product defect, and it is outside the three filing classes. The next face card that touches those harnesses mounts the provider.
